title: How do we check that the figure we built is a rectangle?
description: The finished figure with a side of five centimetres and a diagonal of seven centimetres is checked against the two rules of a rectangle. Keeko's doubt is that measuring one side is enough, and the video breaks it.
teaching_notes: One idea: a figure is a rectangle only if opposite sides are equal in both pairs and all four angles are right angles, so each pair and each corner is checked. Watch for students who measure one side and stop.

source: In the finished rectangle ABCD (DC = 5 cm, diagonal DB = 7 c
video_script.why: A learner checks a drawn figure against the two rules of a rectangle by measuring both pairs of sides and every corner.
video_script.substitution: the finished rectangle ABCD with DC of five centimetres and the diagonal DB of seven centimetres
video_script.anchor: the finished rectangle ABCD with DC of 5 cm and the diagonal DB of 7 cm
video_script.wrong_answer: we should only measure dee cee
video_script.wrong_move: measures one side and assumes the other three sides copy it
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, it is a rectangle. Opposite sides are equal, and all four angles are ninety degrees.

final_answer.value: Yes; AB = DC = 5 cm, AD = BC about 4.9 cm, and all four angles are 90 degrees
final_answer.spoken: yes, it is a rectangle with both pairs of opposite sides equal and all four angles right angles

maths_rules: rule one: opposite sides of a rectangle are equal in length
rule two: all the angles of a rectangle are 90 degrees
AB and DC are both 5 cm
AD and BC are both about 4.9 cm
each corner reads 90 degrees on a set square or a protractor
video_script.design: The finished rectangle stays on the board. A ruler and then a set square move over it, and each reading is ticked beside the side or the corner it belongs to.

<bookmark mark='diag'/>Its side dee cee is five centimetres, and its diagonal dee bee is seven centimetres.
How will you check that it really is a rectangle?

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks we should only measure dee cee, because the other sides will copy it.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But only the opposite side eigh bee copies dee cee.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>The other pair, eigh dee and bee cee, needs its own check.
